source.title: Electrostatic models for zeros of polynomials: old, new, and some open problems

accepted.question_text: Beyond the classical Jacobi, Laguerre, and Hermite cases, can one construct analogous electrostatic models for other families of polynomials in which the zeros are realized as equilibrium configurations of interacting charges under an explicit external field?

evidence.quote: • are there generalizations of these models to other families of polynomials?

accepted.question_text: In electrostatic models for polynomial zeros, must one focus on the global minimum of the total energy, or can other equilibrium notions from the hierarchy discussed earlier—such as other equilibria besides the global minimum—also correspond to the zeros of relevant polynomial families?

evidence.quote: • why necessarily the global minimum of the energy should be considered? Which other types of equilibria described above could be linked to the zeros of the polynomials?

accepted.question_text: When a family of polynomials has nonreal zeros, what is the correct electrostatic model for those complex zeros—namely, what charges, ambient set, and extremal principle should replace the classical real-line picture?

evidence.quote: • what is the appropriate model for the complex zeros (when they exist)?

accepted.question_text: What mathematically meaningful applications do electrostatic models for polynomial zeros have beyond their aesthetic appeal?

evidence.quote: • what kind of applications can these models have beyond their clear aesthetical value?

accepted.question_text: Let p_{2n} be the degree-2n multiple orthogonal polynomial determined by the conditions ∫_{-1}^{0} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)\,dx = ∫_{0}^{1} p_{2n}(x)x^k w(x)\,dx = 0 for k = 0,1,\dots,n-1, where w(x)=x^γ(1-x)^α(1+x)^β with α, β, γ > -1, so that p_{2n} has exactly n zeros in (-1,0) and n zeros in (0,1). Is it true that these two n-point zero sets are equilibrium configurations of positive unit charges subject to mutual logarithmic repulsion, an external field generated by fixed charges α/2, β/2, and γ/2 at 1, -1, and 0 respectively, and n charges of weight 1/2 placed on the opposite subinterval?

evidence.quote: the asymptotic analysis (using the tools of the potential theory) suggests that a reasonable model for these zeros might be that each of these sets of n zeros is the equilibrium position of the positive unit charges, which besides the mutual interaction are subject to the external field generated by the three fixed charges α/2, β/2, γ/2 at 1, −1, 0, respectively, and by the n charges of the weight 1/2 on the other subinterval. Nevertheless, this is an open problem.

accepted.question_text: For Freud-type orthogonal polynomials obtained by perturbing the Freud weight e^{-x^4} with an added fixed charge λ at the origin, do the zeros always form a stable equilibrium, meaning that they realize the global minimum of the total energy, or is there a critical value λ₀(n) such that the zeros minimize the energy only for 0 ≤ λ < λ₀(n) and cease to be stable for λ > λ₀(n)?

evidence.quote: But can we assure that they are in a stable equilibrium, that is, that E(X∗) = min E(X)? The complete answer is not clear yet. By computing the Hessian matrix H (2.9) it was proved that for small values of the correction charge λ this is really the case, but there are some evidences that make it possible to conjecture the existence of a critical value λ0 such that for 0 ≤ λ < λ0(n) the zeros of the orthogonal polynomials attain the minimum of the total energy, but for λ > λ0(n) the equilibrium is no longer stable.

accepted.question_text: Besides being a critical configuration of the energy, do the zeros of the Freud-type orthogonal polynomials preserve any of the other equilibrium notions discussed earlier for classical electrostatic models?

evidence.quote: Is still any other type of equilibria discussed in Section 2 preserved in this case (beside the critical point of the energy)? This is also an open question.

accepted.question_text: For Jacobi polynomials with nonclassical real parameters α and β, can the max-min characterization from Theorem 1 be extended after suitably modifying the admissible family F of continua so that the zeros are still characterized by an extremal problem even in regimes with nonhermitian, multiple, or otherwise nonclassical orthogonality and possibly complex zeros?
accepted.context_brief: Max-min models for nonclassical Jacobi zeros

evidence.quote: We conjecture that Theorem 1 is valid in all these situations after a suitable modification of the family of continua F.
All these facts have been conjectured by one of this authors some time ago, but their proof still remains an open problem.

accepted.question_text: For matrix orthogonal polynomials that satisfy second-order matrix differential equations analogous to the scalar hypergeometric case, can one develop an electrostatic interpretation of their zeros?

evidence.quote: However, a study of the electrostatic interpretation of the zeros of the orthogonal matrix polynomials remains completely open.

accepted.question_text: When Heine-Stieltjes polynomial zeros yield only critical configurations of the discrete energy rather than global minimizers, can one prove that the corresponding discrete critical measures converge in the thermodynamic limit to continuous critical measures, and that every continuous critical measure in the class can be obtained in this way?

evidence.quote: two open problems remain: (i) to prove that discrete critical measures converge in the thermodynamic limit to continuous critical measures, and that all continuous critical measures can be obtained this way;

accepted.question_text: Can one find a feasible description of the multiparametric family of continuous critical measures in the relevant class?

evidence.quote: (ii) to find a feasible description of the multi-parametric family of continuous critical measures in the given class.
